sanskrit: sa vīkṣamāṇas tatrastho mārgamāṇaś ca maithilīm avekṣamāṇaś ca mahīṃ sarvāṃ tām anvavaikṣata
english: Standing there, searching for the daughter of Mithilā, he gazed about and surveyed all the ground around him.

sanskrit: santāna kalatābhiś ca pādapair upaśobhitām divyagandharasopetāṃ sarvataḥ samalaṃkṛtām
english: He beheld it adorned with Santāna and Kalata trees, endowed with divine fragrance and flavor, beautified on every side.

sanskrit: tāṃ sa nandanasaṃkāśāṃ mṛgapakṣibhir āvṛtām harmyaprāsādasaṃbādhāṃ kokilākulaniḥsvanām
english: It resembled Nandana, that grove — thronged with deer and birds, dense with mansions and palaces, filled with the clamorous song of cuckoos.

sanskrit: kāñcanotpalapadmābhir vāpībhir upaśobhitām bahvāsanakuthopetāṃ bahubhūmigṛhāyutām
english: It was beautified by pools bearing golden lotuses and blue water-lilies, furnished with many seats and carpets, and filled with many-storied houses.

sanskrit: sarvartukusumai ramyaiḥ phalavadbhiś ca pādapaiḥ puṣpitānām aśokānāṃ śriyā sūryodayaprabhām
english: Lovely with flowers of every season and fruit-laden trees, it blazed with the splendor of blooming Aśoka trees like the light of sunrise.

sanskrit: pradīptām iva tatrastho mārutiḥ samudaikṣata niṣpatraśākhāṃ vihagaiḥ kriyamāṇām ivāsakṛt viniṣpatadbhiḥ śataśaś citraiḥ puṣpāvataṃsakaiḥ
english: Standing there, the son of Māruta gazed upon it as if blazing — its branches stripped of leaves, made so again and again by birds flying forth in hundreds, wearing blossoms as their garlands.

sanskrit: āmūlapuṣpanicitair aśokaiḥ śokanāśanaiḥ puṣpabhārātibhāraiś ca spṛśadbhir iva medinīm
english: Aśoka trees — destroyers of sorrow — laden with blossoms from root to crown, bowed down by the weight of their flowers as if touching the earth.

sanskrit: karṇikāraiḥ kusumitaiḥ kiṃśukaiś ca supuṣpitaiḥ sa deśaḥ prabhayā teṣāṃ pradīpta iva sarvataḥ
english: With Karṇikāra trees in bloom and Kiṃśuka trees well flowering, that place seemed lit up everywhere by their radiance.

sanskrit: puṃnāgāḥ saptaparṇāś ca campakoddālakās tathā vivṛddhamūlā bahavaḥ śobhante sma supuṣpitāḥ
english: Puṃnāga, Saptaparṇa, Campaka, and Uddālaka trees — many and deep-rooted — shone beautifully, their flowers in full bloom.

sanskrit: śātakumbhanibhāḥ ke cit ke cid agniśikhopamāḥ nīlāñjananibhāḥ ke cit tatrāśokāḥ sahasraśaḥ
english: Some of the Aśoka trees there, thousands of them, resembled burnished gold, some were like tongues of flame, and others were like dark collyrium.

sanskrit: nandanaṃ vividhodyānaṃ citraṃ caitrarathaṃ yathā ativṛttam ivācintyaṃ divyaṃ ramyaṃ śriyā vṛtam
english: Like Nandana, like the variegated garden of Citraratha, it surpassed even the inconceivable — divine, charming, and wrapped in beauty.

sanskrit: dvitīyam iva cākāśaṃ puṣpajyotirgaṇāyutam puṣparatnaśataiś citraṃ pañcamaṃ sāgaraṃ yathā
english: It was like a second sky filled with clusters of floral luminaries, variegated with hundreds of floral gems — like a fifth ocean.

sanskrit: sarvartupuṣpair nicitaṃ pādapair madhugandhibhiḥ nānāninādair udyānaṃ ramyaṃ mṛgagaṇair dvijaiḥ
english: The grove was filled with trees of sweet fragrance flowering in all seasons, charming with diverse calls of herds of deer and birds.

sanskrit: anekagandhapravahaṃ puṇyagandhaṃ manoramam śailendram iva gandhāḍhyaṃ dvitīyaṃ gandhamādanam
english: With currents of many fragrances, sacred in its scent, enchanting to the mind — rich in perfume like Gandhamādana, a second king of mountains.

sanskrit: aśokavanikāyāṃ tu tasyāṃ vānarapuṃgavaḥ sa dadarśāvidūrasthaṃ caityaprāsādam ūrjitam
english: Within that Aśoka grove, that bull among monkeys saw, not far away, a grand sanctuary-palace.

sanskrit: madhye stambhasahasreṇa sthitaṃ kailāsapāṇḍuram pravālakṛtasopānaṃ taptakāñcanavedikam
english: It stood in the center supported by a thousand pillars, white as Kailāsa, its stairways made of coral, its platform of molten gold.

sanskrit: muṣṇantam iva cakṣūṃṣi dyotamānam iva śriyā vimalaṃ prāṃśubhāvatvād ullikhantam ivāmbaram
english: It seemed to steal away the eyes, blazing with splendor, pure and lofty, as if scratching the sky with its height.

sanskrit: tato malinasaṃvītāṃ rākṣasībhiḥ samāvṛtām upavāsakṛśāṃ dīnāṃ niḥśvasāntīṃ punaḥ punaḥ dadarśa śuklapakṣādau candrarekhām ivāmalām
english: Then he saw her — clad in soiled garments, surrounded by rākṣasī women, emaciated by fasting, wretched, sighing again and again — pure as the crescent moon at the start of the bright fortnight.

sanskrit: mandaprakhyāyamānena rūpeṇa ruciraprabhām pinaddhāṃ dhūmajālena śikhām iva vibhāvasoḥ
english: Her beauty, though still alluring, was only faintly visible, like the flame of Agni veiled and obscured by a shroud of smoke.

sanskrit: pītenaikena saṃvītāṃ kliṣṭenottamavāsasā sapaṅkām analaṃkārāṃ vipadmām iva padminīm
english: Clad in a single soiled yellow garment, mud-stained and unadorned — like a lotus pond drained of its lotuses.

sanskrit: vrīḍitāṃ duḥkhasaṃtaptāṃ parimlānāṃ tapasvinīm graheṇāṅgārakeṇaiva pīḍitām iva rohiṇīm
english: Ashamed, tormented by grief, withered, forlorn — like Rohiṇī afflicted by the planet Aṅgāraka.

sanskrit: aśrupūrṇamukhīṃ dīnāṃ kṛśām ananaśena ca śokadhyānaparāṃ dīnāṃ nityaṃ duḥkhaparāyaṇām
english: Her face full of tears, wretched, emaciated by lack of food, absorbed in grief-stricken meditation, pitiable, constantly immersed in sorrow.

sanskrit: priyaṃ janam apaśyantīṃ paśyantīṃ rākṣasīgaṇam svagaṇena mṛgīṃ hīnāṃ śvagaṇābhivṛtām iva
english: Seeing no beloved person, only crowds of rākṣasī women — like a doe separated from her own herd, surrounded by a pack of dogs.

sanskrit: nīlanāgābhayā veṇyā jaghanaṃ gatayaikayā sukhārhāṃ duḥkhasaṃtaptāṃ vyasanānām akodivām
english: A single braid of hair, dark as a black serpent, fallen along her hip — she who deserved only happiness, burned by grief, the very embodiment of calamity.

sanskrit: tāṃ samīkṣya viśālākṣīm adhikaṃ malināṃ kṛśām tarkayām āsa sīteti kāraṇair upapādibhiḥ
english: Observing her — wide-eyed, exceedingly soiled, emaciated — he surmised her to be Sītā, confirming it by the signs he recognized.

sanskrit: hriyamāṇā tadā tena rakṣasā kāmarūpiṇā yathārūpā hi dṛṣṭā vai tathārūpeyam aṅganā
english: For this woman appeared as she had been seen when carried off by that shape-shifting rākṣasa — the very same form.

sanskrit: pūrṇacandrānanāṃ subhrūṃ cāruvṛttapayodharām kurvantīṃ prabhayā devīṃ sarvā vitimirā diśaḥ
english: Her face was like the full moon, her brows lovely, her breasts beautifully rounded — this goddess whose radiance dispelled darkness in all directions.

sanskrit: tāṃ nīlakeśīṃ bimbauṣṭhīṃ sumadhyāṃ supratiṣṭhitām sītāṃ padmapalāśākṣīṃ manmathasya ratiṃ yathā
english: Dark-haired, with lips red as Bimba fruit, slender-waisted, well-proportioned — Sītā with eyes like lotus petals, like Rati to Manmatha.

sanskrit: iṣṭāṃ sarvasya jagataḥ pūrṇacandraprabhām iva bhūmau sutanum āsīnāṃ niyatām iva tāpasīm
english: Beloved of all the world, radiant as the full moon — seated on the earth, slender, as composed as an ascetic.

sanskrit: niḥśvāsabahulāṃ bhīruṃ bhujagendravadhūm iva śokajālena mahatā vitatena na rājatīm
english: Breathing heavy sighs, timid, like the wife of a great serpent-king — not shining, ensnared in a great web of grief.

sanskrit: saṃsaktāṃ dhūmajālena śikhām iva vibhāvasoḥ tāṃ smṛtīm iva saṃdigdhām ṛddhiṃ nipatitām iva
english: Like the flame of fire obscured by a net of smoke — like a memory grown uncertain, like a prosperity that has fallen away.

sanskrit: vihatām iva ca śraddhām āśāṃ pratihatām iva sopasargāṃ yathā siddhiṃ buddhiṃ sakaluṣām iva
english: Like faith that has been struck down, like hope that has been thwarted, like a siddhi beset by obstacles, like an intellect grown turbid.

sanskrit: abhūtenāpavādena kīrtiṃ nipatitām iva rāmoparodhavyathitāṃ rakṣoharaṇakarśitām
english: Like a fame fallen by false slander — afflicted by the anguish of separation from Rāma, wasted by the abduction of the rākṣasa.

sanskrit: abalāṃ mṛgaśāvākṣīṃ vīkṣamāṇāṃ tatas tataḥ bāṣpāmbupratipūrṇena kṛṣṇavaktrākṣipakṣmaṇā vadanenāprasannena niḥśvasantīṃ punaḥ punaḥ
english: Helpless, with eyes like a young deer's, gazing here and there — her dark face with its downcast lashes filled with the water of tears, sighing again and again.

sanskrit: malapaṅkadharāṃ dīnāṃ maṇḍanārhām amaṇḍitām prabhāṃ nakṣatrarājasya kālameghair ivāvṛtām
english: Bearing dirt and grime, wretched, worthy of adornment yet unadorned — like the light of the moon-king veiled by dark clouds.

sanskrit: tasya saṃdidihe buddhir muhuḥ sītāṃ nirīkṣya tu āmnāyānām ayogena vidyāṃ praśithilām iva
english: His mind wavered repeatedly as he gazed upon her — like a sacred science grown slack through disuse.

sanskrit: duḥkhena bubudhe sītāṃ hanumān analaṃkṛtām saṃskāreṇa yathāhīnāṃ vācam arthāntaraṃ gatām
english: With difficulty Hanūmān recognized Sītā unadorned — like a word devoid of proper formation that has drifted to another meaning.

sanskrit: tāṃ samīkṣya viśālākṣīṃ rājaputrīm aninditām tarkayām āsa sīteti kāraṇair upapādayan
english: Observing that wide-eyed, blameless princess, he concluded it was Sītā, establishing it by means of the signs.

sanskrit: vaidehyā yāni cāṅgeṣu tadā rāmo 'nvakīrtayat tāny ābharaṇajālāni gātraśobhīny alakṣayat
english: The ornaments on her limbs that Rāma had described one by one — he now recognized those adornments that beautified her body.

sanskrit: sukṛtau karṇaveṣṭau ca śvadaṃṣṭrau ca susaṃsthitau maṇividrumacitrāṇi hasteṣv ābharaṇāni ca
english: The beautifully crafted ear-ornaments, the Śvadaṃṣṭra jewels well set, and the ornaments on her hands variegated with gems and coral.

sanskrit: śyāmāni cirayuktatvāt tathā saṃsthānavanti ca tāny evaitāni manye 'haṃ yāni rāmo 'vnakīrtayat
english: Darkened now through long wearing, yet retaining their shape — these must be the very ones Rāma described, I believe.

sanskrit: tatra yāny avahīnāni tāny ahaṃ nopalakṣaye yāny asyā nāvahīnāni tānīmāni na saṃśayaḥ
english: Those which are absent I do not see; those which have not been lost — these are they, without doubt.

sanskrit: pītaṃ kanakapaṭṭābhaṃ srastaṃ tad vasanaṃ śubham uttarīyaṃ nagāsaktaṃ tadā dṛṣṭaṃ plavaṃgamaiḥ
english: That auspicious yellow upper garment, bright as a sheet of gold, slipped off and caught in a tree — the one the monkeys had seen at the time.

sanskrit: bhūṣaṇāni ca mukhyāni dṛṣṭāni dharaṇītale anayaivāpaviddhāni svanavanti mahānti ca
english: And the chief ornaments seen on the ground — cast away by her very self, sounding loud and large.

sanskrit: idaṃ ciragṛhītatvād vasanaṃ kliṣṭavattaram tathā hi nūnaṃ tad varṇaṃ tathā śrīmad yathetarat
english: This garment, more worn from long wearing, is nonetheless still of that color — as splendid as the other one.

sanskrit: iyaṃ kanakavarṇāṅgī rāmasya mahiṣī priyā pranaṣṭāpi satī yasya manaso na praṇaśyati
english: This golden-limbed beloved queen of Rāma — even though lost, she does not perish from his mind.

sanskrit: iyaṃ sā yat kṛte rāmaś caturbhiḥ paritapyate kāruṇyenānṛśaṃsyena śokena madanena ca
english: She is the one for whose sake Rāma burns with four fires: compassion, tenderness, grief, and longing.

sanskrit: strī pranaṣṭeti kāruṇyād āśritety ānṛśaṃsyataḥ patnī naṣṭeti śokena priyeti madanena ca
english: Compassion because a woman is lost; tenderness because she was his dependent; grief because his wife is gone; longing because she is his beloved.

sanskrit: asyā devyā yathā rūpam aṅgapratyaṅgasauṣṭhavam rāmasya ca yathārūpaṃ tasyeyam asitekṣaṇā
english: The beauty of this goddess, the perfection of each of her limbs, and the form of Rāma — she of dark eyes is indeed worthy of him.

sanskrit: asyā devyā manas tasmiṃs tasya cāsyāṃ pratiṣṭhitam teneyaṃ sa ca dharmātmā muhūrtam api jīvati
english: This goddess's mind is fixed on him, and his mind is fixed on her — it is for that reason she and that righteous-souled one each live, even for a moment.

sanskrit: duṣkaraṃ kurute rāmo ya imāṃ mattakāśinīm sītāṃ vinā mahābāhur muhūrtam api jīvati
english: Great-armed Rāma does what is difficult indeed — he lives even for a moment without this Sītā whose glance is intoxicating.

sanskrit: evaṃ sītāṃ tadā dṛṣṭvā hṛṣṭaḥ pavanasaṃbhavaḥ jagāma manasā rāmaṃ praśaśaṃsa ca taṃ prabhum
english: Having thus beheld Sītā, the son of Vāyu was overjoyed; in his mind he went to Rāma and praised that lord.

sanskrit: praśasya tu praśastavyāṃ sītāṃ tāṃ haripuṃgavaḥ guṇābhirāmaṃ rāmaṃ ca punaś cintāparo 'bhavat
english: Having praised Sītā who is worthy of all praise, and Rāma who is charming with virtues, that bull among monkeys fell once again into deep reflection.

sanskrit: sa muhūrtam iva dhyātvā bāṣpaparyākulekṣaṇaḥ sītām āśritya tejasvī hanumān vilalāpa ha
english: Having meditated for a moment, his eyes overflowing with tears, the splendid Hanūmān, overcome by his regard for Sītā, lamented aloud.

sanskrit: mānyā guruvinītasya lakṣmaṇasya gurupriyā yadi sītāpi duḥkhārtā kālo hi duratikramaḥ
english: She who is venerable, dear to the elders, honored even by Lakṣmaṇa who is trained by his elders — if even Sītā suffers such grief, truly time is insurmountable.

sanskrit: rāmasya vyavasāyajñā lakṣmaṇasya ca dhīmataḥ nātyarthaṃ kṣubhyate devī gaṅgeva jaladāgame
english: The goddess, knowing the resolve of Rāma and the wise Lakṣmaṇa, is not excessively disturbed — like the Gaṅgā at the onset of rains.

sanskrit: tulyaśīlavayovṛttāṃ tulyābhijanalakṣaṇām rāghavo 'rhati vaidehīṃ taṃ ceyam asitekṣaṇā
english: Equal in character, age, and conduct, equal in lineage and mark — the Rāghava deserves the daughter of Videha, and this dark-eyed lady deserves him.

sanskrit: tāṃ dṛṣṭvā navahemābhāṃ lokakāntām iva śriyam jagāma manasā rāmaṃ vacanaṃ cedam abravīt
english: Seeing her, resplendent as fresh gold, like Śrī beloved of the world, he went to Rāma in his mind and spoke these words.

sanskrit: asyā hetor viśālākṣyā hato vālī mahābalaḥ rāvaṇapratimo vīrye kabandhaś ca nipātitaḥ
english: For the sake of her, this wide-eyed one, the mighty Vālī was slain and Kabandha — equal to Rāvaṇa in prowess — was struck down.

sanskrit: virādhaś ca hataḥ saṃkhye rākṣaso bhīmavikramaḥ vane rāmeṇa vikramya mahendreṇeva śambaraḥ
english: And Virādha, the rākṣasa of terrible might, was slain in battle — by Rāma striding forward in the forest as great Indra slew Śambara.

sanskrit: caturdaśasahasrāṇi rakṣasāṃ bhīmakarmaṇām nihatāni janasthāne śarair agniśikhopamaiḥ
english: Fourteen thousand rākṣasas of terrible deeds were slain at Janasthāna with arrows blazing like tongues of fire.

sanskrit: kharaś ca nihataḥ saṃkhye triśirāś ca nipātitaḥ dūṣaṇaś ca mahātejā rāmeṇa viditātmanā
english: Khara was slain in battle, Triśiras struck down, and the greatly brilliant Dūṣaṇa — by Rāma, the self-realized one.

sanskrit: aiśvaryaṃ vānarāṇāṃ ca durlabhaṃ vālipālitam asyā nimitte sugrīvaḥ prāptavāṃl lokasatkṛtam
english: The sovereignty of the Vānaras, difficult to obtain, guarded by Vālī — for her sake Sugrīva attained it, honored by all the world.

sanskrit: sāgaraś ca mayā krāntaḥ śrīmān nadanadīpatiḥ asyā hetor viśālākṣyāḥ purī ceyaṃ nirīkṣitā
english: The illustrious ocean, lord of rivers and streams, was crossed by me, and this city was reconnoitered — all for the sake of her, this wide-eyed one.

sanskrit: yadi rāmaḥ samudrāntāṃ medinīṃ parivartayet asyāḥ kṛte jagac cāpi yuktam ity eva me matiḥ
english: Even if Rāma were to overturn the entire earth to its ocean-boundary for her sake, the world too would be right — such is my conviction.

sanskrit: rājyaṃ vā triṣu lokeṣu sītā vā janakātmajā trailokyarājyaṃ sakalaṃ sītāyā nāpnuyāt kalām
english: Kingship over the three worlds or Sītā, daughter of Janaka — the whole sovereignty of the three worlds does not match even a fraction of Sītā's worth.

sanskrit: iyaṃ sā dharmaśīlasya maithilasya mahātmanaḥ sutā janakarājasya sītā bhartṛdṛḍhavratā
english: She is the daughter of the virtuous, great-souled king Janaka of Mithilā — Sītā, steadfast in her vow to her husband.

sanskrit: utthitā medinīṃ bhittvā kṣetre halamukhakṣate padmareṇunibhaiḥ kīrṇā śubhaiḥ kedārapāṃsubhiḥ
english: She arose from the earth, from a field furrowed by the plowshare — strewn with auspicious field-dust resembling lotus pollen.

sanskrit: vikrāntasyāryaśīlasya saṃyugeṣv anivartinaḥ snuṣā daśarathasyaiṣā jyeṣṭhā rājño yaśasvinī
english: She is the eldest and glorious daughter-in-law of King Daśaratha — who was valiant, noble in character, and never turned back in battle.

sanskrit: dharmajñasya kṛtajñasya rāmasya viditātmanaḥ iyaṃ sā dayitā bhāryā rākṣasī vaśam āgatā
english: She is the beloved wife of Rāma — who knows dharma, is ever grateful, and is self-realized — now fallen into the power of a rākṣasa.

sanskrit: sarvān bhogān parityajya bhartṛsnehabalāt kṛtā acintayitvā duḥkhāni praviṣṭā nirjanaṃ vanam
english: Forsaking all pleasures, driven by the strength of her love for her husband, giving no thought to hardships, she entered the uninhabited forest.

sanskrit: saṃtuṣṭā phalamūlena bhartṛśuśrūṣaṇe ratā yā parāṃ bhajate prītiṃ vane 'pi bhavane yathā
english: Contented with fruits and roots, devoted to serving her husband — she who found the highest joy even in the forest as if in her own home.

sanskrit: seyaṃ kanakavarṇāṅgī nityaṃ susmitabhāṣiṇī sahate yātanām etām anarthānām abhāginī
english: She, this golden-limbed one who always speaks with a sweet smile — now endures this torment, unlucky in suffering these misfortunes.

sanskrit: imāṃ tu śīlasaṃpannāṃ draṣṭum icchati rāghavaḥ rāvaṇena pramathitāṃ prapām iva pipāsitaḥ
english: Rāghava yearns to see this virtuous woman, afflicted by Rāvaṇa — as a thirsty man yearns for a drinking place.

sanskrit: asyā nūnaṃ punar lābhād rāghavaḥ prītim eṣyati rājā rājyaparibhraṣṭaḥ punaḥ prāpyeva medinīm
english: Surely at regaining her, the Rāghava will find joy — like a king fallen from his kingdom who regains the earth.

sanskrit: kāmabhogaiḥ parityaktā hīnā bandhujanena ca dhārayaty ātmano dehaṃ tatsamāgamakāṅkṣiṇī
english: Abandoned by sensuous pleasures, bereft of her kinsmen, she sustains her body longing for reunion with him.

sanskrit: naiṣā paśyati rākṣasyo nemān puṣpaphaladrumān ekasthahṛdayā nūnaṃ rāmam evānupaśyati
english: She does not see these rākṣasī women, she does not see these trees with their flowers and fruits — her heart fixed in one place, she sees only Rāma.

sanskrit: bhartā nāma paraṃ nāryā bhūṣaṇaṃ bhūṣaṇād api eṣā hi rahitā tena śobhanārhā na śobhate
english: A husband is indeed the supreme ornament of a woman, greater than all ornaments — and deprived of him, she who deserves to shine does not shine.

sanskrit: duṣkaraṃ kurute rāmo hīno yad anayā prabhuḥ dhārayaty ātmano dehaṃ na duḥkhenāvasīdati
english: Rāma, the lord, does what is difficult indeed — bereft of her, he sustains his body and does not sink under grief.

sanskrit: imām asitakeśāntāṃ śatapatranibhekṣaṇām sukhārhāṃ duḥkhitāṃ dṛṣṭvā mamāpi vyathitaṃ manaḥ
english: Seeing her — with dark ends to her hair, eyes like a hundred-petalled lotus, deserving only of happiness yet suffering — even my mind is pained.

sanskrit: kṣitikṣamā puṣkarasaṃnibhākṣī yā rakṣitā rāghavalakṣmaṇābhyām sā rākṣasībhir vikṛtekṣaṇābhiḥ saṃrakṣyate saṃprati vṛkṣamūle
english: Patient as the earth, with eyes resembling a blue lotus, she who was once protected by Rāghava and Lakṣmaṇa — is now guarded at the foot of a tree by rākṣasī women with grotesque eyes.

sanskrit: himahatanalinīva naṣṭaśobhā vyasanaparamparayā nipīḍyamānā sahacararahiteva cakravākī janakasutā kṛpaṇāṃ daśāṃ prapannā
english: Like a lotus-plant struck by frost, its beauty gone, oppressed by a succession of misfortunes, like a Cakravākī separated from her mate — the daughter of Janaka has fallen into a pitiable state.

sanskrit: asyā hi puṣpāvanatāgraśākhāḥ śokaṃ dṛḍhaṃ vai janayaty aśokāḥ himavyapāyena ca mandaraśmir abhyutthito naikasahasraraśmiḥ
english: Indeed, the Aśoka trees whose tips are bent with blossoms evoke a deep sorrow in her; and with winter's departure the sun has risen, his beams no longer mild but blazing in thousands.

sanskrit: ity evam arthaṃ kapir anvavekṣya sīteyam ity eva niviṣṭabuddhiḥ saṃśritya tasmin niṣasāda vṛkṣe balī harīṇām ṛṣabhas tarasvī
english: Having pondered the matter thus, the monkey's mind settled into the certainty that this was indeed Sītā; that mighty, swift bull of the monkeys settled himself in that tree.

sanskrit: tataḥ kumudaṣaṇḍābho nirmalaṃ nirmalaḥ svayam prajagāma nabhaś candro haṃso nīlam ivodakam
english: Then the moon — pure himself, resembling a cluster of Kumuda lotuses — moved through the clear sky, as a swan moves through dark water.

sanskrit: sācivyam iva kurvan sa prabhayā nirmalaprabhaḥ candramā raśmibhiḥ śītaiḥ siṣeve pavanātmajam
english: As if rendering assistance, the moon with pure luster, by his cool rays, served the son of Vāyu.

sanskrit: sa dadarśa tataḥ sītāṃ pūrṇacandranibhānanām śokabhārair iva nyastāṃ bhārair nāvam ivāmbhasi
english: Then he saw Sītā, whose face resembled the full moon, cast down as if by the weight of her grief, like a boat weighed down upon the water.

sanskrit: didṛkṣamāṇo vaidehīṃ hanūmān mārutātmajaḥ sa dadarśāvidūrasthā rākṣasīr ghoradarśanāḥ
english: As Hanūmān, son of Māruta, was eager to behold the daughter of Videha, he saw, not far away, rākṣasī women of terrible aspect.

sanskrit: ekākṣīm ekakarṇāṃ ca karṇaprāvaraṇāṃ tathā akarṇāṃ śaṅkukarṇāṃ ca mastakocchvāsanāsikām
english: One-eyed and one-eared, and others whose ears served as coverings; some with no ears, others with ears like pegs; some with nostrils set on top of the head.

sanskrit: atikāyottamāṅgīṃ ca tanudīrghaśirodharām dhvastakeśīṃ tathākeśīṃ keśakambaladhāriṇīm
english: Some with enormous bodies and large heads, others with thin and long necks; some with disheveled hair, some bald, others wearing a blanket of hair.

sanskrit: lambakarṇalalāṭāṃ ca lambodarapayodharām lambauṣṭhīṃ cibukauṣṭhīṃ ca lambāsyāṃ lambajānukām
english: Some with pendulous ears and forehead, pendulous belly and breasts, pendulous lips or chin-like lip, pendulous face and pendulous knees.

sanskrit: hrasvāṃ dīrghāṃ ca kubjāṃ ca vikaṭāṃ vāmanāṃ tathā karālāṃ bhugnavastrāṃ ca piṅgākṣīṃ vikṛtānanām
english: Short and tall, hunchbacked and deformed, dwarfish and frightful, crooked in garment, tawny-eyed, with disfigured faces.

sanskrit: vikṛtāḥ piṅgalāḥ kālīḥ krodhanāḥ kalahapriyāḥ kālāyasamahāśūlakūṭamudgaradhāriṇīḥ
english: Misshapen, tawny, dark-complexioned, wrathful, fond of quarrel — bearing great iron spears, clubs, and maces.

sanskrit: varāhamṛgaśārdūlamahiṣājaśivā mukhāḥ gajoṣṭrahayapādāś ca nikhātaśiraso 'parāḥ
english: Some with faces of boar, deer, tiger, buffalo, goat, and jackal; others with the feet of elephant, camel, and horse; some with sunken heads.

sanskrit: ekahastaikapādāś ca kharakarṇyaśvakarṇikāḥ gokarṇīr hastikarṇīś ca harikarṇīs tathāparāḥ
english: One-handed and one-footed, some with ears like a donkey's or a horse's, others with ears like a cow's or an elephant's, and yet others with ears like a lion's.

sanskrit: anāsā atināsāś ca tiryan nāsā vināsikāḥ gajasaṃnibhanāsāś ca lalāṭocchvāsanāsikāḥ
english: Some noseless, others with oversized noses, some with sideways noses, others entirely without nostrils; some with elephant-like noses, some with nostrils on their foreheads.

sanskrit: hastipādā mahāpādā gopādāḥ pādacūlikāḥ atimātraśirogrīvā atimātrakucodarīḥ
english: Some with elephant's feet, some with great feet, some with cow's feet, some with feet like tufts; some with excessively large heads and necks, others with excessively large breasts and belly.

sanskrit: atimātrāsya netrāś ca dīrghajihvānakhās tathā ajāmukhīr hastimukhīr gomukhīḥ sūkarīmukhīḥ
english: Some with excessively large mouths and eyes, with long tongues and nails — some with faces of a goat, elephant, cow, or sow.

sanskrit: hayoṣṭrakharavaktrāś ca rākṣasīr ghoradarśanāḥ śūlamudgarahastāś ca krodhanāḥ kalahapriyāḥ
english: Rākṣasī women of terrible appearance with faces of horse, camel, and ass — bearing spears and clubs in their hands, wrathful, delighting in strife.

sanskrit: karālā dhūmrakeśīś ca rakṣasīr vikṛtānanāḥ pibantīḥ satataṃ pānaṃ sadā māṃsasurāpriyāḥ
english: Terrible and smoke-haired rākṣasī women with disfigured faces, constantly drinking, always fond of flesh and wine.

sanskrit: māṃsaśoṇitadigdhāṅgīr māṃsaśoṇitabhojanāḥ tā dadarśa kapiśreṣṭho romaharṣaṇadarśanāḥ
english: Their bodies smeared with flesh and blood, feeding on flesh and blood — those were the ones that best of monkeys saw, dreadful to behold, causing the hair to stand on end.

sanskrit: skandhavantam upāsīnāḥ parivārya vanaspatim tasyādhastāc ca tāṃ devīṃ rājaputrīm aninditām
english: Seated around a great shouldering forest tree, encircling it — and beneath it that blameless goddess and princess.

sanskrit: lakṣayām āsa lakṣmīvān hanūmāñ janakātmajām niṣprabhāṃ śokasaṃtaptāṃ malasaṃkulamūrdhajām
english: The auspicious Hanūmān fixed his gaze on the daughter of Janaka — lustrous no longer, scorched by grief, her hair matted and filthy.

sanskrit: kṣīṇapuṇyāṃ cyutāṃ bhūmau tārāṃ nipatitām iva cāritrya vyapadeśāḍhyāṃ bhartṛdarśanadurgatām
english: As if a star fallen to earth with exhausted merit — rich in the renown of her virtue yet reduced to misery by separation from her husband's sight.

sanskrit: bhūṣaṇair uttamair hīnāṃ bhartṛvātsalyabhūṣitām rākṣasādhipasaṃruddhāṃ bandhubhiś ca vinākṛtām
english: Deprived of her finest ornaments, yet adorned by her husband's love — confined by the lord of rākṣasas, separated from all her kin.

sanskrit: viyūthāṃ siṃhasaṃruddhāṃ baddhāṃ gajavadhūm iva candralekhāṃ payodānte śāradābhrair ivāvṛtām
english: Separated from her herd, hemmed in by a lion, like an elephant cow in bondage — like the crescent of the moon veiled at the edge of clouds by autumn clouds.

sanskrit: kliṣṭarūpām asaṃsparśād ayuktām iva vallakīm sītāṃ bhartṛhite yuktām ayuktāṃ rakṣasāṃ vaśe
english: Her beauty worn away from lack of touch, like a lute neglected and unplayed — Sītā, devoted to her husband's welfare, unfitting to be under the dominion of rākṣasas.

sanskrit: aśokavanikāmadhye śokasāgaram āplutām tābhiḥ parivṛtāṃ tatra sagrahām iva rohiṇīm dadarśa hanumān devīṃ latām akusumām iva
english: In the midst of the Aśoka grove, plunged in an ocean of grief, surrounded by those rākṣasī women — like Rohiṇī seized by a planet — Hanūmān saw the goddess, like a creeper stripped of its flowers.

sanskrit: sā malena ca digdhāṅgī vapuṣā cāpy alaṃkṛtā mṛṇālī paṅkadigdheva vibhāti ca na bhāti ca
english: Her body smeared with grime, yet adorned by natural beauty — like a lotus-stalk besmeared with mud, she both shines and does not shine.

sanskrit: malinena tu vastreṇa parikliṣṭena bhāminīm saṃvṛtāṃ mṛgaśāvākṣīṃ dadarśa hanumān kapiḥ
english: The monkey Hanūmān saw that radiant one, doe-eyed, wrapped in a soiled and worn garment.

sanskrit: tāṃ devīṃ dīnavadanām adīnāṃ bhartṛtejasā rakṣitāṃ svena śīlena sītām asitalocanām
english: That goddess with a wretched face, yet inwardly undaunted, protected by her husband's glory and by her own virtue — Sītā of dark eyes.

sanskrit: tāṃ dṛṣṭvā hanumān sītāṃ mṛgaśāvanibhekṣaṇām mṛgakanyām iva trastāṃ vīkṣamāṇāṃ samantataḥ
english: Seeing Sītā, with eyes resembling those of a young deer, frightened like a young doe, gazing in all directions —

sanskrit: dahantīm iva niḥśvāsair vṛkṣān pallavadhāriṇaḥ saṃghātam iva śokānāṃ duḥkhasyormim ivotthitām
english: — as if scorching with her sighs the trees bearing new shoots, like a mass of sorrows embodied, like a wave of anguish arisen —

sanskrit: tāṃ kṣāmāṃ suvibhaktāṅgīṃ vinābharaṇaśobhinīm
english: — emaciated, yet with well-proportioned limbs, beautiful even without ornaments —

sanskrit: praharṣam atulaṃ lebhe mārutiḥ prekṣya maithilīm harṣajāni ca so 'śrūṇi tāṃ dṛṣṭvā madirekṣaṇām mumoca hanumāṃs tatra namaś cakre ca rāghavam
english: — the son of Māruta felt an incomparable joy on beholding the daughter of Mithilā; and seeing her of intoxicating eyes, Hanūmān shed tears born of joy, and there he bowed to the Rāghava.

sanskrit: namaskṛtvā ca rāmāya lakṣmaṇāya ca vīryavān sītādarśanasaṃhṛṣṭo hanūmān saṃvṛto 'bhavat
english: And having bowed to Rāma and to Lakṣmaṇa, that mighty Hanūmān, exhilarated at the sight of Sītā, composed himself.
